resources.string: If you take any medicine, ask your pharmacist or doctor before you use it.
An infusion: pour the hot water over it and let it steep.
A decoction: simmer it in the water.
A small book of herbs for tea: who should not take each one, what it is traditionally used for and what the research says, and how to make it. It works without a connection.

This app is a reference book, not medical advice. It cannot tell you that an herb is safe for you. Herbs can interact with medicines and can harm some people, in pregnancy and nursing especially. If you take any medicine, are pregnant or nursing, or are unwell, ask your doctor, midwife or pharmacist first. See a doctor for anything serious or lasting.

The cautions and the research lines are written from the US National Center for Complementary and Integrative Health\'s Herbs at a Glance pages (nccih.nih.gov) and, for comfrey, from LiverTox (National Institute of Diabetes and Digestive and Kidney Diseases). Both are works of the US government and in the public domain; the wording in this app is its own. Each herb\'s page lists its sources. The herb text is still a draft.

Nothing you do in the app leaves this phone. The app has no internet permission and cannot go online. \"Feed the llamas\" in About, and a source\'s address on an herb page, open in your browser only when you press them.
There are no ads, no analytics and no tracking.
